titleEn: Toes Slide In, Heel Goes Down!

pages.text: "I'll put them on myself!" At the porch's edge, Yuki pulled over the boots. The yard was muddy from overnight rain. One boot's heel was folded inward.
"I'll put them on alone and splash in the mud today!" Yuki pushed a foot in, but the toes caught halfway.
Yuki jumped off the porch anyway. One step, two steps in the mud—the foot kept slipping out. Yuki wobbled and limped.
Squelch! The boot stuck in the mud, and the foot came out. Yuki's sock was soaked. "I can't play..." Back on the porch, Yuki hung their head.
Grandma lifted the boot to show Yuki and straightened its folded heel. "A boot is a tunnel. A folded tunnel won't let your foot through."
"When your toes reach the tunnel's end, your heel drops down." Grandma sang, "Toes Slide In, Heel Goes Down!" Yuki lifted their chin. Getting dressed suddenly became a game.
Yuki held the boot upright with both hands and slid the toes far in. When they reached the end, the heel dropped down. "It's in!"
Now the other boot! Toes slide in, heel goes down! Yuki stamped at the porch's edge. Thump, thump—neither boot came off. Brown dog Momo wagged hard nearby.
Yuki adjusted the scarf knot neatly. "One, straighten the tunnel! Two, toes slide in! Three, heel goes down!" Yuki jumped into the mud and played as much as they liked.

Grandma lifted Yuki from the mud and pressed cheeks together. "You can put them on yourself now!" A boot was a tunnel for the toes to pass through first. Yuki swung both feet, splashing mud. "Toes Slide In, Heel Goes Down!"
